name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,579

clue.text: Might they make one better-looking?

blocks.note: surface reading: beauticians or stylists who improve someone's appearance
setter's reading: making someone better at looking, that is, helping them see more clearly with glasses

explanation.surface: A question about who could make a person more attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'better-looking' as 'better at looking': the professionals are the eye specialists who fit spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Opticians test eyesight and supply glasses or contact lenses, which improve how well a customer can see.

clue.text: Exactly where you might beat The Hammers?

definitions.text: Exactly where you might beat The Hammers?

blocks.note: surface reading: defeating West Ham United, the London football club nicknamed The Hammers
setter's reading: the spot that hammers strike, the head of a metal pin, and an idiom meaning precisely

explanation.surface: A football fan asks precisely where their team could defeat West Ham.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hammers is the nickname of West Ham United, a London football club; read literally, hammers beat a nail on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely or immediately, especially of payment, and hammers literally strike a metal pin there.

clue.text: Head of theology on drugs will show bit of leg

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of theology is kept

blocks.note: first letter of theology
someone on drugs is high

explanation.surface: A theology professor under the influence ends up showing some leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper section of the human leg, between hip and knee.

clue.text: Wake up and rue condom bursting

indicators.note: something bursting breaks apart, so its letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone surfaces from sleep only to regret a split contraceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round is to regain consciousness, as after fainting or anaesthesia, much like waking.

clue.text: Ring nun late in a state

indicators.note: being in a state means agitated and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone phones a nun who is running behind and getting flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulet is a small circular band, used in heraldry and architecture as a decorative moulding.

clue.text: Uphold university mark after end of appeals

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of appeals is kept
after places the university and mark pieces behind the letter from appeals

blocks.note: last letter of appeals
U is the standard abbreviation for university
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: A university's reputation is upheld, or blemished, once the appeals process is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an objection or ruling is to support and confirm it, as a judge does.

clue.text: Change a lawyer gets with pint

blocks.note: taken as written
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: A lawyer's fee is paid in loose change and a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to alter or modify something to suit new conditions, a verb meaning to change.

clue.text: A little problem sending off first letter

indicators.note: sending off the first means dismissing the opening letter of the word for a small problem

blocks.note: taken as written
a hitch is a small snag or difficulty

explanation.surface: A minor snag occurs when the first letter is sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter removed from hitch is H, and the answer is the name of that very letter, which neatly ties wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelled-out name of the eighth alphabet character, H.

clue.text: Ache and groan wandering around city abroad

indicators.note: wandering around means roaming aimlessly, so these letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footsore tourist aches and groans while wandering around a foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska, so it lies overseas from Britain, where the clue was set.

clue.text: Son visiting art gallery shows good judgement

indicators.note: someone visiting goes inside a place, so one piece sits within the gallery's name

blocks.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son's trip to an art gallery reveals his discerning eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the ability to discern quality and appropriateness, especially in aesthetic matters.

clue.text: What usually comes with awfully grim mist shrouding north

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters come out in a muddled order
shrouding means wrapping around, so the jumbled letters enclose the compass point

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A gloomy fog descends over the northern landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: the side dishes and garnishes that usually accompany a main dish, such as a roast turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmings are the traditional accompaniments served alongside a main dish, so they are what usually goes with it.

clue.text: Drunk heading back round a Cafe's front for food

indicators.note: heading back means travelling the opposite way, so the word for a drunk is read right to left
the front of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Cafe's is kept
round means encircling, so the backwards drunk goes around the other letters

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
taken as written
first letter of Cafe's

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers home via a cafe to grab something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are Mexican folded tortillas with fillings, an everyday snack or meal.

clue.text: English chap cuddling tense Republican? Heavens!

indicators.note: cuddling means snuggling up close, so the chap is pressed tight against the letter for tense

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a chap is a male, referred to as he
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An Englishman embracing an anxious Republican provokes a shocked exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are not in clue order: tense is cuddled up just in front of the chap, between him and the English letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a poetic term for the clear upper sky or the celestial regions, the heavens.

clue.text: Criminal shot a mole - that's abhorrent

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal lover condemns someone who illegally shot a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means causing hatred or disgust, a close synonym of repugnant and detestable.

clue.text: A crack about Tory leader being in the wrong

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening of Tory is kept
about means surrounding, so the phrase for a crack goes around the letter from Tory

blocks.note: a fault is a crack, as in a geological fracture
first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A rift has opened around the Conservative leader, who is blamed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: At fault means responsible for a mistake or blameworthy, the same as being wrong.

clue.text: Glow that comes from unstable fuel cores

indicators.note: something unstable cannot hold its form, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about the eerie light from a nuclear reactor's failing fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluoresce is to emit visible light after absorbing radiation, a verb for shining or glowing.

clue.text: Game PM's address brought round party

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so the number of the address is read backwards

blocks.note: the British Prime Minister lives at Number 10 Downing Street
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's speech is brought round to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a speech, but it is the PM's home address, 10 Downing Street, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, where players shoot through a high hoop.

clue.text: Will trial with a group of chaps lead to trouble?

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of trouble is kept

blocks.note: a test is a trial
taken as written
chaps are men
first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A worried question whether a legal case over a will may cause friction among the men.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament, as in 'last will and testament', is a legal document leaving property after death.

clue.text: What a seaborne invasion will do for the army?

definitions.text: What a seaborne invasion will do

blocks.clueFragment: What a seaborne invasion will do
blocks.note: first meaning: put troops ashore, as a verb phrase
second meaning: the military branch fighting on the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the first is a verb and the second its object; read as one phrase, it is a noun for ground troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphibious assault delivers troops ashore, and the same phrase names a nation's ground-based military service.

clue.text: Peer over top of unmade beds regularly to see a sacred place!

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the peer is draped around the letter from unmade
the top of a word is its first letter, so only the start of unmade is kept
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of beds is taken

blocks.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
first letter of unmade
second and fourth letters of beds

explanation.surface: A nosy aristocrat inspects the messy beds of a holy site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning to look closely, but it is a noun for a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes, in southwest France, is a Catholic pilgrimage town famed for its Marian shrine.

clue.text: Struck with top of southpaw’s boxing glove

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of southpaw's is kept

blocks.note: first letter of southpaw's
a boxing glove, like a mitten, has no separate fingers

explanation.surface: A left-handed boxer lands a blow with his glove.
explanation.walkthrough: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, which keeps the whole surface in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the past participle of smite, meaning hit hard, as in 'smitten by a blow'.

clue.text: Recognise research group after review of small papers

indicators.note: a review looks back over something, so these letters are read in the other direction
after places the research group behind the turned letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
ID means identity papers
CERN is the European particle physics research organisation near Geneva

explanation.surface: A scientist identifies a research team after peer review of short scientific papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or detect something, making out or identifying it.

clue.text: Depressing high toll overwhelms hospital department

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the toll wraps around the department

blocks.note: a ding is the high ringing sound of a bell's toll
ENT is the Ear, Nose and Throat department

explanation.surface: A grim report says a high death toll has swamped a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressing' looks like an adjective for gloomy, but it means pressing down; 'toll' is not a death count but a bell ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Denting means pressing a hollow into a surface, which is depressing it in the physical sense.

clue.text: Infusion over pan is steaming

indicators.note: steaming suggests agitation or heated motion, so these letters are churned around

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: an infusion simmers over a pan that is steaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Pervasion is the spreading through every part of something, just as an infusion permeates a substance.

clue.text: Religious bigwigs take pills and ecstasy tabs

blocks.note: to pop pills is to swallow them
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so several are Es

explanation.surface: Church leaders caught taking pills and party drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Popes are heads of the Roman Catholic Church, the most senior figures in that faith.

clue.text: Bill navy after installing bit of outside deck

indicators.note: installing means fitting one thing inside another, so the bill and navy close around the extra letter
a bit of a word here is its first letter, so only the start of outside is kept

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
first letter of outside
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Bill joins the navy after fitting part of a ship's outer deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, but here it is a verb meaning to decorate, as in 'deck the halls'.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn is to decorate or embellish, as in decking a room with ornaments.

clue.text: A place to go with female that's pretty distant

blocks.note: taken as written
loo is British slang for a toilet, the place you go when you need to go
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman's toilet is located some way off.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof describes someone cool and reserved, emotionally remote and standoffish.

clue.text: Fungal spores found in Hanoi diabetic

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A medical report of spores discovered in a diabetic patient in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Oidia are thin-walled asexual spores produced by certain fungi, the plural of oidium.

clue.text: I annoy constantly with bit of obscene sauce

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter, so only the start of obscene is kept

blocks.note: someone who annoys constantly is a pest
first letter of obscene

explanation.surface: A confession from a persistent nuisance who adds a dash of filthy lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' sounds like cheek or rude backchat, fitting the obscene annoyance, but it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian blend of basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and olive oil served with pasta.

clue.text: Trouble cutting easy to chew batter?

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the trouble goes inside the word for easy to chew

blocks.note: tender meat is soft and easy to chew
to ail is to trouble, as an illness does

explanation.surface: A cook struggles to slice a soft batter-coated dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' looks like the cooking mix, but it is a cricket batsman; a tail-ender bats last and is usually the weakest, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a tail-ender is one of the lowest-order players, usually a bowler with limited skill.

clue.text: Mug fools about, having drunk last of wine

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for fools is read backwards
the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of wine is kept
having drunk means taking something inside, so the reversed fools swallow the letter from wine

blocks.note: nits are idiots, short for nitwits
last letter of wine

explanation.surface: Idiots messing about with a mug after finishing the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' could mean a dupe, matching the fools, but it is the drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer tankard, a type of drinking vessel.

clue.text: I got eaten by mistake in Deal

indicators.note: a mistake puts things out of their proper place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims they were accidentally devoured in Deal, a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' is capitalised to look like the Kent town, but it is the verb for doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate is to bargain or conduct talks, as in dealing with another party.
